title: User scope install upgrade leaves old version info behind

judgment.rationale: A second user reports that old-version files trigger repeated security detections, strengthening the impact evidence. The surviving entries still need to be distinguished from actual side-by-side installations before proposing cleanup.
evidence: The report describes silent per-user winget upgrades leaving 0.95, 0.97 and 0.101 entries.
A manual 0.102 installer removed the immediate 0.101 predecessor but left older entries, confirmed in the installed-app list.
The report does not establish that all displayed versions still have runnable installations.
A second user reports that their organization's security software repeatedly flags old-version files after upgrades; the detected file and whether it still exists are not identified.

Upstream main 9e6593c34949: installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/Product.wxs: current authoring uses MajorUpgrade, UpgradeCodeGUID and PREVIOUSVERSIONSINSTALLED detection; that alone does not establish how old bootstrapper registrations are removed.
Read the upgrade command history and manual-install control. No registry deletion or installation was performed.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce installer upgrade inventory behavior and correlate the reported security detection with the surviving installation entry.

fix_assessment.rationale: Conditional lightweight proposal, not an implementation-grade design. The old-versus-immediate-predecessor behavior is concrete, but surviving entry ownership has not been inventoried.

proposed_fixes.title: Reconcile stale related-product registrations across upgrade generations
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Older upgrade generations may leave stale ARP/bootstrapper registrations outside the immediate predecessor detected by the current installer. Actual side-by-side binaries and scope history remain unverified.
plan: On a disposable account, reproduce the reported per-user winget version chain and then the manual-current-installer control.
Record related MSI/bundle identities, scope, uninstall target and installed executable versions for each surviving entry.
Fix the proven related-product detection/removal gap; remove only identified obsolete registrations through supported installer ownership, not broad registry deletion.
verification: Only the expected current product remains after the reproduced chain and repair.
Per-user and system installations are not conflated, and unrelated products/user settings are preserved.
Manual installation, upgrade and uninstall continue to work.

confidence.rationale: The old-versus-immediate-predecessor behavior is concrete, but surviving entry ownership has not been inventoried.

The report does not establish that all displayed versions still have runnable installations.

issue_context.analysis: The additional report establishes a security-tool impact but not whether the detection refers to a live old executable or stale product metadata. Preserve the distinction between orphaned registrations and genuine side-by-side installations before recommending installer cleanup.

Re-read the November 6 comment reporting outdated-install detections. It does not name the detected file/version or say whether the file still exists; do not infer that the report is caused by an ARP entry alone.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Share only the detection name, file version and yes/no presence of the file and Installed-app entry. Redact usernames and full local paths; do not attach organization-specific security reports.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes an active outdated binary from stale uninstall metadata and identifies which upgrade generation or installation scope must be investigated.
information_gaps.information: The security product's detection name and detected file version, whether that file still exists, and whether the corresponding old PowerToys entry remains in Installed apps

comment.body: Thanks for the additional report that security software is flagging old PowerToys files after upgrades. To distinguish an outdated binary from stale uninstall metadata, could you share the security product's detection name and detected file version, whether that file still exists, and whether the corresponding old PowerToys entry remains in Installed apps? Please omit organization-specific reports and redact usernames or full local paths.

reproduce.title: Validate installer upgrade inventory report
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable release; compare the reported version only in an isolated test environment if needed.
prerequisites: Use a disposable test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: Recreate the reported per-user winget upgrade chain in a disposable account.
For each remaining app entry, compare bundle/MSI identity, installation scope, uninstall target and live executable version.
Apply the current manual installer and compare which related entries it removes; do not delete registry entries to manufacture a clean result.
reproduce.expected_result: Determine whether entries are orphan registrations or real installations and identify the upgrade generation that retains them.
